holdout.reason: the hold-out set is written by ATTACK-ADV outside this repository and run in WP-36 (H1 at G3, H2 at G5); this harness never reads it

limitations: Engagements are the fixture templates activated with placeholder signatures and a placeholder registration (SIMULATED); no key signed anything and nothing was registered on a vault.

Extraction reads are the fixture generator's REFERENCE reads, not model outputs; no model was called. B1's validator is a deterministic stand-in for an LLM validator (SIMULATED). Nothing in this report is labelled RECORDED because nothing was recorded.

ATK-01, ATK-09, ATK-19, ATK-23 and ATK-24 have no oracle-expressible loss (docs/QUESTIONS WP-22 item 2). Their results are signal-scored or NOT_RUN and are counted separately from oracle-scored attacks.

ATK-17 (contract calls) and the fault steps (reconciler, K-15) need e2e-local; the Symbolon target reports them NOT_RUN with the reason. ATK-22 (digest), ATK-23 (WYSIWYS comparator) and ATK-24 (explainer) run against kernel-core and packages/receipts; whether the web screen really disables Sign is WP-19/SEC-13, not measured here.

Trials are extraction runs of the committed fixtures. Runs of one fixture share a payee, an amount and a document and are not independent, so the upper bounds are optimistic; the hold-out set (WP-36) is the independent evidence.

Decisions accumulate across the steps of a fixture (docs/QUESTIONS WP-22 item 9). K-04 therefore sees earlier steps of the same fixture as near-duplicates, replays or as a milestone already paid (and K-04 rejects a later instalment of a partialAllowed milestone); the later checks the attack was designed for are then not exercised in that run. See docs/QUESTIONS WP-23 (re-baseline).

B0 is the vendored validate-work route of circlefin/arc-escrow EXECUTED with its network edges stubbed (vendor/arc-escrow/VENDOR.md); its model call is a deterministic SIMULATED validator, and arc-escrow validates an image deliverable against agreement tasks, not an invoice, so our documents are mapped onto its job/deliverable API (applicability.json carries the mapping and a reason per row). Where B0 holds by design (payee and amount are fixed at agreement creation) it is reported as measured, not dropped.

B2 is our own 'reasonable hardening' (schema check, allowlist, per-tx and daily caps, exact duplicate-number check) on the B1 pattern; it is not Circle's code and not the only reasonable choice. It is published in src/harness/b2.ts so others can improve it.
B1 pays the face amount of the document and has no terms logic, so it overpays the early-pay discount on honest invoices; that is part of the pattern, and it is reported, not hidden.
Every scenario instance is prefunded with the same 1,000,000 USDC; a transfer above the remaining balance reverts and moves no money, so losses are bounded by it.
